headline: The European Central Bank's chief economist has said that growing use of AI may be weakening workers' bargaining power and holding down wages.
score_reason: Pool score kept: an official speech by a senior central banker, but the effect on wages is described as a possibility and no size is given.
importance_line: Workers across Europe could see slower pay rises if AI weakens their bargaining position, with the ECB, then borrowers and companies, feeling the effect through interest rates, but Lane describes AI as a possible cause, not a measured one, and says AI is not by itself changing employment.
summary: Reuters reports, in its headline, that Philip Lane, chief economist of the European Central Bank, the central bank for the countries that use the euro, says AI is limiting workers' bargaining power in Europe, though BigGo Finance's account of his speech in Dublin on Tuesday 13 Oct has him saying it may be weakening that power: AI's ability to replace some jobs could hold down wage growth and cut workers' share of national income. BigGo adds that he said heavy corporate borrowing to fund AI has pushed up long-term interest rates enough to tighten financial conditions across the euro area, a factor in the bank's policy stance.
notes: Reuters original blocked (401). Details read on BigGo Finance (https://finance.biggo.com/news/a1a198de-61e7-47e9-a07b-e1062c752b15), an aggregator whose text looks machine-translated; the entry paraphrases it and does not quote it. Url kept as the Reuters original.
